description: Seal in fine-grained yellow steatite with a deep cut inscription, but no device (Plate XIX, fig. 15).
source: Daya Ram Sahni, 1926. Annual Report of the Archaeological Survey of India 1923-24, pg 53.

description: Square, bossed faience sealing with double triangles in fields on either side of the diagonal line (Pl. XCV, 400).
source: Madho Sarup Vats, Excavations at Harappa (1940), pgs 24, 347; Sahni 1926, pg 53, Pl. XIX, 16.
type: a (square seal with perforated boss on reverse)

description: Rectangular, plano-convex steatite seal (No. Ab553, Pl. XCII, 274).
source: Madho Sarup Vats, Excavations at Harappa (1940), pgs 23, 343; Sahni 1926, pg 53, Pl. XIX, 17.
type: c (rectangular seal with plane face and convex back)

description: Bears the figure of a unicorn standing to left and an inscription in the same 'Indo-Sumerian characters as are found on other seals from Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.'
source: Daya Ram Sahni, 1926. Annual Report of the Archaeological Survey of India 1923-24, pg 53, Pl. XIX, 18.
type: a (square seal with perforated boss on reverse)

description: Half of a square faience sealing inscribed with a double square (Pl. XCV, 394).
source: Madho Sarup Vats, Excavations at Harappa (1940), pgs 23, 347; Sahni 1926, pg 53, Pl. XIX, 19.
type: a (square seal with perforated boss on reverse)
